[README.md > What you get]
Every dataset is a folder with the same three files, and your app loads only these:

- `network.json`: systems, facilities, wells, tanks, pumps, pipelines and disposal sites.
- `ops.json`: prices, repair times and trucks.
- `telemetry.csv`: the sensor readings coming from everything in the network.

| Folder | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `history/full_week/` | One week of a network (systems S1 to S5), plus `answer_key.json`: every event, when it started and ended, and the plan that should have been used |
| `history/snapshot_*/` | The same week cut off at three earlier moments, with problems still in progress, each with its own `answer_key.json` |
| `history/mock_test_*/` | The same week cut off once more, with **no** answer key: a dress rehearsal for judging |
| `test/` (added right before judging) | A week from a **different network** (S6 to S11) you have never seen. Three files, no answer key |

`answer_key.json` is for checking your app, never for loading into it. [history/README.md](history/README.md) explains each folder and how to read the answer key.

[SPEC.md > The three problems]
| Category | What happens |
|---|---|
| `pipeline_leak` | Water escapes from the pipeline. Doesn't fill a tank, so no countdown. Gets `field_inspection` |
| `pump_degradation` | The pump wears out and moves less water over time. Doesn't fill a tank, so no countdown. Gets `field_inspection` |
| `pump_failure` | The pump stops working. Its tank fills until the repair is done or the tank reaches `shutdown` |

**How each one shows up in the readings is for you to work out.** Start by comparing the readings during the labelled events in `history/full_week/answer_key.json` with the readings outside them.

[history_README.md > Reading the answer key]
`answer_key.json` lists every event that has started by "now", in onset order.

- `status`: `resolved` or `ongoing`. Every event in `full_week/` is `resolved`. An ongoing event has a null `end`, because the operator doesn't know yet when the repair will finish.
- `reference_action`: the cheapest plan (see [SPEC.md](../SPEC.md#plans)).
- Pump failures: `trips_at` is when the tank reached, or will reach, its shutdown limit if nobody acts. In a snapshot, ongoing ones also give `level_final_pct` and `hours_to_limit_final`, the tank level and countdown at "now", and their `reference_action` is planned from "now".
- When several pumps in one system fail together, each is its own event with its own countdown. Their `reference_action`s are planned together, because they share the system's trucks, and a note says which events they share with.
- Snapshots only: each ongoing pump failure has an `order`, its place in the alerts view ([SPEC.md](../SPEC.md#alerts-view)): soonest `hours_to_limit_final` first, with `lost_revenue_per_hour` as the tie-break. Leaks and worn pumps have no `order`; they follow the pump failures in any order.

[SPEC.md > network.json]
| Level | Contains |
|---|---|
| System | Facilities, one disposal site, truck yard, map center |
| Disposal site | Where every pipeline in the system ends and the water goes underground. Location and `pressure_psi` only. It has no sensors and never goes down |
| Facility | Lat/long, wells, one tank, one pump, and one pipeline to its system's disposal site |

Key fields: `capacity_bbl` (tank size), `start_level_pct` / `stop_level_pct` (pump setpoints), `max_flow_bpd` (a healthy pump's flow while running), `warning` / `shutdown` (tank limits in `defaults.tank_limits_pct`, the same for every tank), and each well's `baseline_water_bpd`, `oil_bpd`, `gas_mcfd`.

[SPEC.md > Normal behavior]
The tank level makes a sawtooth. The pump starts at `start_level_pct`, stops at `stop_level_pct`, and keeps its state in between. Level change per hour is `(inflow − pump flow) ÷ 24 ÷ capacity × 100`.

[SPEC.md > Plans]
```
lost revenue per day = oil_bpd × prices.oil_per_bbl + gas_mcfd × prices.gas_per_mcf
shut-in cost         = lost revenue per hour × hours shut in
cost per bbl avoided = lost revenue per day ÷ baseline_water_bpd
```

**Doing nothing** is allowed. The automatic shut-in then costs the facility's total lost revenue per hour for as long as it is shut. Plans can mix, for example one truck now plus a late shut-in of a cheap well.

**Horizon:** `expected_repair_hours.pump_failure`. For an ongoing event, it is the repair time remaining at "now".

**Shared trucks.** A system's `emergency_fleet_size` covers every problem in that system at once.

- At "now", nothing has been dispatched yet (the data is a recording with no operator actions), so all of a system's ongoing pump failures share its whole fleet. Plan them together: a truck sent to one tank can't help another.
- In `full_week/answer_key.json`, each event's `reference_action` is planned at its onset, assuming earlier reference plans were followed. A truck sent to an earlier event stays busy until it's back from its last trip, so a later event in the same system may find no trucks free.

# Domain Brief: Industrial Oil/Water Production Network Monitoring

**Sources:** `SPEC.md`, `network.json`, `examples.md`, `history_README.md`. All numbers traced to these sources.

---

## 1. Equipment & Sensors

| Component | Key Fields / Metrics | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **System** (S1–S5; test: S6–S11) | Facilities, one disposal site, truck yard, map center | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| **Facility** | One tank, one pump, one pipeline, wells (oil/water/gas), lat/long | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| **Tank** | `capacity_bbl` (barrels), `start_level_pct`, `stop_level_pct` (pump setpoints), `warning`/`shutdown` percent limits from `defaults.tank_limits_pct` (same for every tank) | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| **Pump** | `max_flow_bpd` (healthy pump flow while running) | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| **Wells** (per facility) | `baseline_water_bpd`, `oil_bpd`, `gas_mcfd` | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| **Disposal Site** | `pressure_psi` only; never goes down, no other sensors | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| **Telemetry** | `timestamp, ts_unix, asset_id, metric, value` — sampled every 5 min (`ts_unix` +300 per step; base `1791158400` = `2026-10-05T00:00:00Z`) | `examples.md` |
| **Pipeline (to disposal)** | Implicit flow/pressure metrics; healthy `pressure_psi` referenced above | `SPEC.md` |

---

## 2. Normal Operation (Sawtooth Cycle)

- Pump **starts** when tank level hits `start_level_pct`, **stops** at `stop_level_pct`.
- Tank level change per hour: `(inflow − pump_flow) ÷ 24 ÷ capacity × 100` (SPEC.md).
- Healthy pump flow: `max_flow_bpd` (barrels/day) while running.
- Well baselines sustained continuously: `oil_bpd`, `gas_mcfd`, `baseline_water_bpd` per facility.
- Pipeline to disposal site maintains steady `pressure_psi`; never triggers alarms in healthy state.
- Telemetry rows: one reading per 5-min step per asset; `metric` column encodes the type (e.g., `tank_level_pct`, `pump_flow_bpd`, `pipeline_pressure_psi`, `well_oil_bpd`, etc.).

---

## 3. Problem Signatures — Physical Effect + Reading Changes

### `pump_failure`
- **What happens:** Pump stops. Inflow continues → tank level rises steadily.
- **Reading changes:**
  - `tank_level_pct` rises toward `shutdown` limit (percent) without pump `on/off` cycling; may trigger at `trips_at` level recorded in `answer_key.json`.
  - `pump_flow_bpd` drops to 0 or reads abnormally low.
  - `pump_status` changes to stopped/idle.
- **Key numbers:** `shutdown` threshold from `defaults.tank_limits_pct`; `trips_at` level (% ) in practice answer keys; `capacity_bbl` determines rate of rise.

### `pipeline_leak`
- **What happens:** Water escapes from the pipeline before reaching the tank.
- **Reading changes:**
  - `pipeline_pressure_psi` drops below normal operating pressure (healthy baseline from disposal site section).
  - Tank fill rate stalls or decreases unexpectedly (inflow reduced).
  - No countdown: docs explicitly say "Doesn't fill a tank, so no countdown." Action: `field_inspection`.
  - `tank_level_pct` may show irregular fill pattern or slower rise.
- **Key numbers:** Healthy `pressure_psi` from `network.json` disposal site; deviation from baseline signals leak.

### `pump_degradation`
- **What happens:** Pump wears out, moves less water over time (gradual, not sudden).
- **Reading changes:**
  - `pump_flow_bpd` shows a downward trend relative to `max_flow_bpd` baseline (gradual decline over days/weeks).
  - Tank fill rate slows → `tank_level_pct` rise rate decreases per the hour-change formula, but still cycles between `start_level_pct`/`stop_level_pct`.
  - No countdown: docs say "Doesn't fill a tank, so no countdown." Action: `field_inspection`.
- **Key numbers:** `max_flow_bpd` as healthy baseline; rate of decline inferred from successive telemetry `value` entries; `capacity_bbl` modulates visible level change speed.

---

## 4. Key Ranges & Baselines Summary

| Metric | Healthy Range / Baseline | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tank level cycle | Between `start_level_pct` and `stop_level_pct`; sawtooth per hour-change formula | `SPEC.md` |
| Pump flow | `max_flow_bpd` while running; 0 when stopped/failing | `SPEC.md` |
| Pipeline pressure | `pressure_psi` at disposal site; never goes down in healthy operation | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| Tank shutdown limit | `shutdown` percent from `defaults.tank_limits_pct` (shared across all tanks) | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| Well baselines | `oil_bpd`, `gas_mcfd`, `baseline_water_bpd` per facility | `SPEC.md > network.json` |
| Telemetry sampling | Every 5 min; `ts_unix` increments of 300; base 1791158400 = 2026-10-05T00:00:00Z | `examples.md` |

---
*All numbers and field names are drawn from `SPEC.md` and `network.json`. `answer_key.json` is practice-only and not loaded by the monitoring app.*
